findings.text: blocking: tests/test_the_orchestrator_reset_row_says_what_it_is.py is outside the dispatch's enumerated write paths, so promotion's scope check refuses this node until the coordinator grants the path; plan section 9's write-path clause grants it and the edit is required because that file pinned the superseded wording.

non-blocking: the job-cell padding added in 8575a8ebca has no assertion behind it; neither test file compares a reset row's column positions against a fleet or lift row, so reverting the cell to elide(_job_name(...), NODE) leaves all 21 tests passing.

non-blocking: assert rendered.split()[1] == ticker.LIMIT_STAGE compares the stage cell against the renderer's own constant, so a change to that constant moves both sides together even though it still separates the reset path from the lift path.

item_verdicts.diff: read commit by commit from 90c8167f1592 to d091a650371d; 8575a8ebca pads the reset row's job cell through _job_cell and replaces constant-valued wording assertions with literals, d091a65037 corrects the evidence fragment's figures and its account of the module-width failure; 4 files, all inside the plan's write paths.
item_verdicts.done_when: the done_when asks for a follower-driven case whose stage cell reads limit and whose line carries limits reset, continue and worker lanes keep their limits with no transition; tests/test_a_limit_reset_reaches_every_pane.py:192-211 is that case and the manifest records its run.
item_verdicts.goal: the source node's goal is that a reset row tells orchestrator sessions to continue and opens no worker lane; the gained commits reckon/crew/ticker.py:3176-3185 keep that row and now pad its job cell, so the goal still holds at the reviewed head.
item_verdicts.manifest: read; it records base 1 failed 16 passed and head 1 failed 17 passed on the node suite, the 24-file sweep at 159 against 160 passed, the negative control at 3 failed 11 passed EXIT=1, and names every log.
item_verdicts.write_paths: the dispatch fenced four paths; the gained commits also touch tests/test_the_orchestrator_reset_row_says_what_it_is.py, which plan section 9's write-path clause grants as another test asserting the superseded row but the dispatch fence does not name, and the worker records that deviation in evidence_inputs.

justifications.durability: tests/test_the_orchestrator_reset_row_says_what_it_is.py:135 now pins the literal words rather than ticker.RESET_ORCHESTRATOR_INSTRUCTION, so a wording change reddens it, but nothing guards the job-cell padding added at reckon/crew/ticker.py:3183.
justifications.evidence: the base and head logs under the reviewed run's logs/ carry their revisions, module paths, cwd and EXIT= lines, and their summaries read 1 failed 16 passed against 1 failed 17 passed with the same failure id.
justifications.fit: the change routes the reset row through the same _job_cell call the fleet row at reckon/crew/ticker.py:3080 and the lift row at :3224 already use, and no added name is forbidden.
justifications.goal_fidelity: reckon/crew/ticker.py:3176-3185 composes the reset row from its own fields and the resolved wallet, so a claude-orchestrators reset prints the orchestrator instruction and every reset row still closes with the worker-lane clause.
justifications.reuse: no new definition is added; the reset row reuses _job_cell at reckon/crew/ticker.py:2942 rather than forking a second fitting mechanism, and the search over reckon/crew found no other job-cell owner.
justifications.scope_discipline: every path in the gained commits is inside plan section 9's write paths, but tests/test_the_orchestrator_reset_row_says_what_it_is.py:132 lies outside the dispatch's enumerated fence, which the worker reports rather than hides.
